job_description: Leading the ISDL Z AI Performance Team, driving strategic Generative AI innovation for IBM Z systems. Built LogSense — a Multi-Agentic AI Log Analysis Platform powered by IBM Bob — reducing manual log triage time by 70% and reclaiming 1,000+ engineering hours annually. Also developed an AI Talent Acquisition Suite that reduced hiring cycle time by 50%. Developed strategic AI roadmaps for IBM Z AI performance initiatives and led cross-functional alignment with global IBM Research teams (US & Germany). Driving AI adoption across IBM ISDL India by identifying high-impact use cases, promoting automation-led productivity gains, and championing responsible AI practices.
summary: I'm currently leading the Z AI Performance team at IBM Research Labs in Bangalore. Our focus is on making generative AI and large language models work reliably at enterprise scale, especially on IBM’s specialized accelerators like Spyre and Telum. One of the projects I’m most proud of is the real-time credit card fraud detection system we built on Telum II for the z17 platform. It now processes 481 billion inferences every day at sub-millisecond latency and was featured in IBM’s commercial launch — directly contributing to revenue growth this year. Seeing something move from an idea in the lab to part of IBM’s flagship hardware was a big moment for the team. Before this, I led GenAI and LLM initiatives at Grid Dynamics for clients including Apple R&D and PepsiCo, delivering multimodal RAG and multi-agent systems with a 100% on-time record. Earlier at Intel Labs, I worked on AI workload optimization using OneAPI tools and helped improve OpenVINO’s NLP capabilities. Those experiences taught me both the technical depth needed to make AI production-ready and the practical challenges of getting it adopted by real teams. What I’ve enjoyed most over the last few years is the leadership side of the work — building and mentoring teams (including groups of research interns), creating internal tools like LogSense that have saved engineers over a thousand hours, and aligning people across locations. I regularly collaborate with teams in the US, Germany, and India. I’ve learned that scaling AI effectively isn’t just about models and accelerators. It’s also about building trust, setting clear priorities, and helping talented people do their best work. I’m at a point where I want to grow as a leader who can connect deep technical work with broader business outcomes and responsible AI practices. I’m particularly interested in opportunities that let me take more ownership of strategy and cross-functional delivery while staying close to the technology. Open to conversations around enterprise GenAI infrastructure, team building, and scaling these systems responsibly.

summary: Mechanical engineer with nine years in oil and gas, eight of them at ONGC across offshore operations and, currently, machinery procurement and projects.I spent over five years offshore on a process complex in the Western Offshore Basin, working hands-on with the machines that keep production running — gas turbines driving process gas compressors and turbo generators, centrifugal and water injection pumps, screw compressors, and the diesel engines behind fire water and emergency power.
